source: tool_descriptions.en.v1.json with every Spanish example and word in English (ING5, 2026-11-13)

tools.app.close: Close an open application gracefully, never force-killing it: by appId (as in app_open), all its windows; by windowId (from window_resolve or window_active, never invented; it expires after 5 minutes: invalid_or_expired_window_id), that one window. A window answering with its own dialog (saving) stops it: close_prompted. Use when: the person asks to close an app or its window (the app, or its window when it has one: appId as is, no window_resolve first; one window the person singles out: its windowId, from window_active for this one or window_resolve for one among several). Do not use when: every window of the desktop (use window_close_all), force-killing a hung program (use system_process_terminate_named), a web page (use browser_control). Examples: «close spotify», «close this window» (window_active gives its windowId), «close chrome».
tools.app.installed: Check whether a normal application is installed on this PC, in the Windows Start catalog, without opening it; a name the catalog does not list comes back inStartCatalog false (programs outside Start are not seen), with the closest catalog names. Use when: the request is a question about an app being installed. Do not use when: the person wants it opened (use app_open), the target is a game (use game_installed_named), or asks if it is open right now (use window_application_status). Examples: «do I have zoom installed?», «is discord installed?», «is obs installed?».
tools.app.open: Open an application or game launcher by name (Steam, Epic Games, Discord, Spotify, Notepad, Calculator) and verify its window appeared; the result says whether it is in front (foreground) and, if not, which window holds the front. Use when: open/launch/start an app or launcher. Do not use when: asking if installed (use app_installed or game_installed_named), playing a game (use game_launch), playing music or video (use media_play_query or streaming_play_named), an already open window (use window_focus), a file (use file_open), opening Word to write a text you compose (use office_document_create, then file_open to show it). Examples: «open steam», «open discord for me», «open spotify». Set foreground true so the person sees it, and forControl true; set forControl false only when the person asks to run it as administrator. place opens a section of the app directly, with no clicks: {app_places}. placeValue is what to search when the place is a search (the person's own words, a topic or a kind of game is enough, e.g. «horror»), and the game's name, as the person said it, for game. newDocument true opens a new blank document in the app; without it Word, Excel and the other Office apps stay on their start screen, with no document, where the only text field is the search box. Look at the window afterwards to see where it arrived.
tools.app.restart: Restart an open app: its windows close gracefully as with app_close (never forced; a dialog of its own, such as saving, stops it: close_prompted), its processes must end within 10 s (app_kept_running if it stays running hidden; never killed), then app_open opens it again; only a new process counts (else app_restart_not_verified). appId as in app_open. Use when: restart or relaunch an app, or close it and open it again (one call, not app_close then app_open). Do not use when: the PC (use system_power). Examples: «restart the calculator», «restart vlc», «restart it» right after an app was opened (that app).
tools.assistant.status: Read BAXY's own state, what it uses or sent: scope version, BAXY's installed version; scope confirmation, its confirmation mode, normal (it asks the person's yes before a risky call) or bypass (it runs them without asking); scope model, the video memory and RAM its model takes; scope internet, what left for the internet in this session, each with its destination and time. Do not use when: the PC's memory (use system_status), turning bypass off (use system_settings_set). Examples: «what version of BAXY do you have?», «are you in bypass mode?», «how much memory are you using?», «what went out to the internet in this session?».
tools.audio.app.volume.adjust: Raise or lower one application's volume (its mixer slider) by an amount from its current level; master volume untouched. Only applications playing on the default output are found. Use when: an app is named with raise/lower/more/less, with or without an amount. Do not use when: an exact target level (use audio_app_volume_set), no app named (use audio_volume_adjust). Examples: «turn spotify down by 20», «raise discord's volume by 10», «turn down chrome by 15».
tools.audio.app.volume.set: Set one application's volume (its mixer slider) to an exact level 0-100, even while paused; master volume untouched. Only applications playing on the default output are found. Use when: an app is named with a target number or percent. Do not use when: raising or lowering by an amount (use audio_app_volume_adjust), no app named (use audio_volume), muting one application (use audio_mute with scope app). Examples: «set spotify to 30», «discord at 50 percent», «set chrome volume to 20».
tools.audio.device.list: List the active sound outputs (speakers, headphones, headsets) and inputs (microphones) by the names Windows shows, and which one is the default of each, without changing anything. Use when: the person asks which sound devices there are or which one is in use. Do not use when: the volume or mute state (use audio_status). Examples: «what sound outputs do I have?», «which headphones are connected?».
tools.audio.device.set: Make one active sound output the default (or an input, with kind input), chosen by its name, and read the default back. If no name or several names match, nothing changes and the result lists the devices: ask which one. Use when: the person asks to switch where the sound comes out (or which microphone is used) to a device they name. Do not use when: the volume (use audio_volume), muting (use audio_mute), Discord's own microphone (use client_microphone_set). Examples: «switch to the Kestrel headphones» (device Kestrel), «put the sound through the Vantor speakers» (device Vantor), «switch the output to the Lumo speakers» (device Lumo), «use the Strato microphone» (kind input, device Strato).
tools.audio.microphone.mute: Mute or unmute the default microphone (sound input), the one in use: it takes no name. Use when: the person mentions the microphone or mic. Do not use when: asking whether it is muted (use audio_microphone_status), muting the speakers, the headphones, an application or any other name said as what to silence (use audio_mute), the microphone inside Discord (use client_microphone_set), the sound of a Discord call (use client_deafen_set). Examples: «mute the microphone», «turn the mic back on», «mute the mic».
tools.audio.microphone.status: Read whether the default microphone (sound input) is muted, without changing anything. Use when: the person asks if the microphone or mic is muted or on. Do not use when: muting or unmuting it (use audio_microphone_mute), the speakers or headphones (use audio_status), the microphone inside Discord (use client_microphone_set). Examples: «is my microphone muted?», «is my mic on?».
tools.audio.mute: Mute or unmute sound output: all of the PC's sound (scope pc: the speakers, headphones or headset), or one application's own sound (scope app, with its name in app; the rest keeps sounding). Use when: silence, mute or unmute. Do not use when: the microphone (use audio_microphone_mute), the sound of a Discord call only (use client_deafen_set), pausing what plays (use media_control), changing the level (use audio_volume or audio_volume_adjust). Examples: «silence the pc» (scope pc), «silence the speakers» (scope pc), «mute spotify» (scope app, app spotify), «unmute it» (scope pc), «mute the sound» (scope pc). Silencing never turns anything off.
tools.audio.status: Read which audio output is in use, its volume and whether it is muted, without changing anything. Use when: the person asks the current volume or where the sound comes out. Do not use when: changing the volume (use audio_volume or audio_volume_adjust), asking which song plays (use media_status). Examples: «what's the volume at?», «where is the sound coming out?», «is the pc muted?».
tools.audio.volume: Set the PC master volume to an exact level 0-100. Use when: a target number or percent is given («to 50», «at 40», «at 30»), even with the verb raise/lower. Do not use when: raising or lowering by an amount from the current level (use audio_volume_adjust), one app only (use audio_app_volume_set), muting (use audio_mute). Examples: «set the volume to 50», «volume at 20», «raise the volume to 80», «lower it down to fifteen» (level 15), «turn it up to seventy» (level 70).
tools.audio.volume.adjust: Raise or lower the PC master volume by an amount from its current level: «down 10» ends 10 lower, «down to 10» ends at 10 (that one is audio_volume). Use when: raise/lower/more/less with no level to end at, with or without an amount. Do not use when: a number after «to», «at», «up to» or «down to» is the level to end at, even with raise or lower (use audio_volume), one app only (use audio_app_volume_adjust). Examples: «raise the volume 10», «lower the volume by 20», «turn it down by 5».
tools.backup.create: Make a private backup copy of one file of BAXY's work folder already identified (resource id and hash, as filesystem_list gives them); the person's own folders are backed up whole with backup_known_create. Its SHA-256 is checked against the original and recorded. Use when: backing up a single file found earlier. Do not use when: a whole known folder (use backup_known_create), zipping (use file_compress). Examples: «make a backup of that file», «make a backup copy of that report in the work folder», «back up that file».
tools.backup.known.create: Create a ZIP backup of a known folder (desktop, documents, pictures or projects; all_known is desktop, documents and pictures, not projects) with its manifest; the written ZIP's hash is read back, its entries are not compared with the folder again. Not in it: reparse points (OneDrive placeholders, links), files it cannot open (held by another program, without permission, or gone meanwhile), folders it cannot open and anything past 32 levels; skippedReparsePointFiles, skippedReparsePointFolders and skippedUnreadableFiles count the first three (the rest is uncounted). With nothing copied it fails: known_backup_nothing_readable (files found that could not be copied) or known_backup_nothing_copied (none found where it could look), never saying the folder is empty. Use when: backing up or a backup of a whole folder. Do not use when: backing up one single file (use backup_create), just zipping a file or folder next to itself (use file_compress). Examples: «make a backup of documents», «back up the desktop», «backup of my pictures».
tools.backup.known.list: List the ZIP backups of known folders and re-verify that they are intact (20 by default). A view shows 20 at most (truncated, …Shown; the rest is not reached). Use when: asking which folder backups exist. Do not use when: backups of single files (use backup_list). Examples: «what folder backups do I have?», «show me the documents backups», «list my folder backup copies».
tools.backup.known.restore.latest: Restore the most recent ZIP backup of a known folder by extracting it into a new separate folder; the original is not overwritten. Use when: recovering or restoring a folder backup. Do not use when: only checking integrity (use backup_known_verify_latest), a single-file backup (use backup_restore). Examples: «restore the latest documents backup», «recover the desktop backup», «restore my pictures backup».
tools.backup.known.verify.latest: Check that the most recent ZIP backup of a known folder is intact (SHA-256), without restoring it. Use when: asking whether a folder backup is OK. Do not use when: restoring it (use backup_known_restore_latest), a single-file backup (use backup_verify). Examples: «verify the latest documents backup», «is the desktop backup OK?», «check the pictures backup».
tools.backup.list: List the private backups of single files, newest first, each saying whether it still has the SHA-256 recorded when it was made. 20 by default (totalCount says how many there are). A view shows 20 at most (truncated, …Shown; the rest is not reached). Use when: asking about backups of individual files. Do not use when: ZIP backups of whole folders (use backup_known_list). Examples: «which files do I have backed up?», «list the file backups», «show me the copies of single files».
tools.backup.restore: Restore a single-file backup into a free path of BAXY's private work folder (sandbox); a backup changed since it was made, or without its recorded SHA-256, is not restored. Use when: recovering a file backup listed earlier. Do not use when: a folder ZIP backup (use backup_known_restore_latest). Examples: «restore that backup copy», «recover the copy of the report», «restore that backup».
tools.backup.verify: Check that a private single-file backup is intact (its SHA-256 against the one recorded when it was made), without restoring it. Use when: asking whether one file backup is OK. Do not use when: a folder ZIP backup (use backup_known_verify_latest), restoring it (use backup_restore). Examples: «verify that backup», «is the copy of the report intact?», «check that backup».
tools.baxy.exit: Close BAXY itself, as «Quit» in its tray icon's menu does: the conversation is kept, the icon goes and its voice and model stop until the person opens it again (it cannot open itself back). Only that the request reached the App is known (delivered). Use when: the person asks BAXY to close, quit, exit or turn itself off for good. Do not use when: closing another application (use app_close), the PC (use system_power), only being quiet or stopping what it says (answer in one word), silencing its proposals or its voice (use baxy_settings_set). Examples: «close yourself», «quit yourself», «exit BAXY».
tools.baxy.settings.set: Change one of BAXY's own settings: its voice (off: BAXY stops speaking aloud and keeps answering in text), its overlay (the small window in a corner that shows what BAXY does while its window is behind), the accessible mode of its own window (larger text, more contrast, bigger buttons), its web search (off: BAXY does not search the internet; on: it may again), weather, looking at the screen, not interrupting during games, calls or videos, silencing its proposals (its own suggestions) for 30m, 1h or until tomorrow (on ends the silence), its wake sound, ignoring what the PC plays, saying «One moment», telling about new versions, staying in the tray on close or minimize, its Bypass mode (confirmation_bypass: on asks the person's yes itself), its language (language: spanish or english: the language BAXY's own rules, screen and answers are in; it restarts by itself when the reply ends and the conversation starts anew) or its tool profile (tool_profile: esencial, diario, avanzado or completo, which tools it has; it restarts by itself when the reply ends). Do not use when: the PC's sound (use audio_mute) or Windows settings such as brightness, dark mode or do-not-disturb (use system_settings_set). Examples: «mute your voice», «be quiet but keep answering in writing», «hide the overlay», «turn on accessible mode», «you can search the internet now», «don't suggest anything to me until tomorrow», «switch to the Diario profile», «change the language to English», «switch to Spanish».
tools.baxy.routines: Open BAXY's own step-by-step setup of a routine: BAXY then asks the person what it needs, one question at a time, and saves it only with their «yes». A routine is a word of theirs that stands for an order («when I say X, do Y») or a text BAXY says aloud at a time. It takes no arguments and by itself does and saves nothing: call it alone, with no other tool for that request. Use when: the person asks to make or set up a routine, in any words, with or without the word «routine»: they want something done from now on each time they say a word of theirs («I want you to do Y every time I say X», "make it so that when I say X, Y happens"). BAXY can do that, and only through this call: never answer that it cannot, and never answer that it is set up without this call. Do not use when: the person says «give me a reminder…» or «remind me…», or asks for an alarm, a timer or a wake-up, also when it repeats every day or on some days (use schedule_alarms); the person asks for something now (call its tools).
tools.baxy.update: Check whether there is a newer version of BAXY itself where it was published (action check), or update BAXY to it (action install: on GitHub it downloads BAXY's installer and the engine asks the person's yes itself before it opens it, and BAXY closes while it is replaced; on Steam or itch.io the store updates BAXY by itself and this opens its page). When the person asks BAXY to update itself, call install directly: it says when there is nothing newer. Do not use when: the person asks to update Windows, a driver, a game or another application (BAXY does not do that: say so). Examples: «BAXY, update», «is there a new version of BAXY?», «update yourself».
tools.bluetooth.device.list: List the Bluetooth devices Windows knows, connecting none: the paired ones (paired true), on or in range now or not, and unpaired ones it found (canPair: whether they can be paired). It does not tell which are near or connected. A view shows 20 at most (truncated, …Shown; the rest is not reached). Use when: asking which Bluetooth devices there are. Do not use when: pairing one (use bluetooth_device_pair), asking whether Bluetooth is on (use bluetooth_radio_status), wired peripherals (use peripheral_list). Examples: «what bluetooth devices are there?», «look for bluetooth headphones», «list the bluetooth devices».
tools.bluetooth.device.pair: Pair an already identified Bluetooth device through Windows' own pairing dialog and permission. Pairing is not connecting: a device already paired comes back paired true without being connected, and BAXY has no tool that connects one. Use when: pairing or linking a Bluetooth device. Do not use when: only listing devices (use bluetooth_device_list), turning Bluetooth on (use bluetooth_radio_set). Examples: «pair my headphones», «link the bluetooth speaker», «pair the jbl».
tools.bluetooth.radio.set: Turn the PC's Bluetooth radio on or off. Use when: turn on/turn off/enable/disable bluetooth. Do not use when: only asking its state (use bluetooth_radio_status), Wi-Fi (use wifi_radio_set), airplane mode for all radios (use system_settings_set). Examples: «switch on the bluetooth», «turn off the bluetooth», «turn on bluetooth».
tools.bluetooth.radio.status: Read whether Bluetooth is on or off, without changing it. Use when: asking about the Bluetooth state. Do not use when: switching it (use bluetooth_radio_set), listing devices (use bluetooth_device_list). Examples: «is bluetooth turned on?», «do I have bluetooth enabled?», «is the bluetooth on?».
tools.browser.control: Act on the active tab of the person's own default browser (its front window): back, reload, scroll up or down, a new empty tab (it opens no link), fullscreen video or leave it (exit_fullscreen), close the page or all pages but the last (closing the last would close the window: with one tab nothing is closed and the result says so). To close a tab that is not the active one, name it in tab; the result says which tab went (closedTab) and every tab left (remainingTabs), as the strip read after shows them. To go to another tab, closing nothing, use switch_tab with its name in tab; the result says the tab now active (activeTab) and the others (otherTabs). close_all stops after 50 tabs or 40 seconds (user_browser_close_all_incomplete; closedTabs says how many). user_browser_history_start: the active tab has no earlier page to go back to (that tab only, not the browser). Use when: the person refers to the current page. Do not use when: a new address (use browser_navigate), opening a link or result shown on the page (look at the browser window with input_visible_controls, then input_visible_click on it), scrolling a non-browser window (use input_pointer_control), closing another app (use app_close). Examples: «go back», «scroll down the page», «reload the page», «exit full screen», «close the runpod tab» (close, tab «runpod»), «switch me to the outlook tab» (switch_tab, tab «outlook»).
tools.browser.navigate: Go to an exact web address in the person's browser; also open a search-results page there when the engine or browser is named as the place («search for it on Google»). Use when: a URL or site is given. Do not use when: a browser is named (use browser_navigate_named), an answer is wanted (use web_search), a YouTube video should play (use media_play_youtube). Examples: «open youtube.com», «go to wikipedia.org», «look it up on google». Never use it to reach a section of a desktop application that is open on screen (a library, a tab, a settings page): that is app_open with place when the section is one of its places, otherwise input_visible_click on its label.
tools.browser.navigate.named: Open a web address in a named browser: Opera, Opera GX, Chrome, Edge or Brave. Use when: the person names one of those browsers as where the page opens. Do not use when: no browser is named (use browser_navigate), only the browser app is wanted with no page (use app_open). Examples: «open youtube in opera gx», «open gmail in chrome», «open netflix.com in edge».
tools.browser.page.read: Read the title, address and visible text of the page in front in the person's own default browser (or in BAXY's own browser while a session of it is open), without touching it: up to 6,000 characters (maximumCharacters can ask for fewer; truncated says when it was cut). Use when: asking what the current page says or to summarize it. Do not use when: a PDF or text file (use file_read), searching the internet (use web_search), listing tabs (use browser_tabs_list). Examples: «what does this page say?», «summarize the page for me», «read the open web page».
tools.browser.tabs.list: List the tabs of the person's own default browser (its front window), with their titles and, when the browser says it, which one is active (20 by default). A view shows 20 at most (truncated, …Shown; the rest is not reached). Use when: asking which tabs or browser tabs are open. Do not use when: reading one page's text (use browser_page_read), asking which app window is in front (use window_active). Examples: «what tabs do I have open?», «list the tabs», «show me the tabs».
tools.calculator.expression.evaluate: Type a simple arithmetic expression into the open Windows Calculator and read the result it displays. Use when: the person asks to compute something in the Calculator, or asks the open Calculator for an operation («do a multiplication» right after opening it). Do not use when: the Calculator should only be opened (use app_open), or a question asks only for the number («how much is…?»), even with the Calculator open (calculate). Examples: «calculate 25 times 4 in the calculator», «use the calculator for 120 divided by 3», «add it up in the calculator: 15 plus 27». expression: numbers (at most 12 digits before the point and 6 after) with + - * /; ^ and parentheses only in Scientific mode, which follows precedence; no function (no root, logarithm or other) in any mode; Standard mode applies each operator in the order typed, so «(12+8)*3» is written «12+8*3» there (it shows 60). It acts on the Calculator that is open, in Standard or Scientific mode (the result says which); with none open it opens it first and the result says so (applicationOpened), and if it cannot, nothing is pressed (calculator_window_not_found: then app_open); in another mode, calculator_mode_not_supported. Starting with a number clears the display first; starting with an operator («+53») continues from the number it shows.
tools.calendar.event.create: Create an event with a title, start time and end time in the person's Outlook calendar (Outlook syncs it to their account when the account syncs; the result reads it back on this PC). Use when: scheduling a meeting or appointment with a time span. Do not use when: something must ring or remind at a time (use schedule_alarms), a to-do (use task_create). Examples: «schedule a meeting tomorrow from 3 to 4», «create an event on Friday from 10 to 11», «dentist on the calendar on Monday from 9 to 10».
tools.calendar.event.list: List the events of Outlook's default calendar between two dates or times at most 366 days apart (longer is refused, calendar_range_invalid), changing nothing (other accounts and calendars are not read): at most 200 are read (truncatedAt200 past them), and a view shows the first 20 (eventsShown; the rest is not reached). Use when: asking what is on the calendar or agenda: meetings today, the next meeting. Do not use when: alarms or reminders (use schedule_alarms), tasks (use task_list). Examples: «what's on my calendar tomorrow?», «show me my events for this week», «do I have meetings today?».
tools.capture.active.window: Take a screenshot of only the active window; optionally also save it as PNG in a known folder (pictures puts it into its Screenshots folder). Use when: the capture is of this window or the current app. Do not use when: the whole desktop (use capture_screenshot), reading or describing the screen (use ocr_read or vision_describe after a capture). Examples: «capture the active window», «take a picture of this window», «screenshot of this window».
tools.capture.screenshot: Take a screenshot of the whole desktop; optionally also save it as PNG in a known folder (desktop, documents, downloads, or pictures, where it goes into its Screenshots folder). Use when: screen capture, screen grab or screenshot without limiting it to one window. Do not use when: only the active window (use capture_active_window). Examples: «take a screen capture», «grab the screen and save it to the desktop», «take a screenshot».
tools.client.channel.locate: Search Discord's quick switcher for a channel or chat by name and say whether a row with exactly that name appears (found compares the row's name before its first comma; a direct chat's row carries the account after the name, so for a chat read switcherRows, the rows as shown), joining or opening nothing. The switcher is closed only while Discord stays in front with the focus in it; on success, a switcher it did not close (switcherNotClosed) or Discord left shown is said; a failure after the shortcut only says an effect may have occurred (switcher or Discord may be left open); with no rows read the result is not_read, never «no such channel». Use when: whether a Discord channel or chat exists. Do not use when: writing a message (use message_draft), opening Discord (use app_open). Examples: «look for the general channel on discord», «is the music channel on discord?», «find the memes channel on discord».
tools.client.channel.open: Open a conversation or channel by its name in Discord or WhatsApp, writing nothing, and read back that it is the one on screen. Use when: the person wants to see or go to a chat, a direct message or a server's channel without sending anything (open, go into, show me). Do not use when: writing or sending a message (use message_draft or message_send), only whether a Discord channel exists (use client_channel_locate), opening the app itself (use app_open). Examples: «open Pedro's chat on discord», «go into the music channel of the Gamers server», «show me the conversation with Lucía on whatsapp». Discord opens the first quick-switcher result holding the name (never a voice channel's row) and counts it open only if the window title is that name (a server's channel: the channel, then its server); WhatsApp opens only a chat named exactly so (with none or several, the chat list's names come back as candidates). When it is not verified, what the title or header showed comes back as headerRead and that chat may stay open.
tools.client.deafen.set: Deafen or undeafen the person inside Discord, by Discord's own deafen button, and read back both states: deafened true stops every sound of Discord's calls reaching the person and, in Discord, also mutes their microphone (micMuted says it after); false gives the call's sound back. Use when: the person names Discord and what they hear from it or its call (deafening, deafen, the call's audio or sound), off or back on. Do not use when: only their own microphone in Discord (use client_microphone_set), the PC's sound or microphone (use audio_mute or audio_microphone_mute). Examples: «deafen me on discord», «undeafen me on discord».
tools.client.microphone.set: Mute or unmute the person's own microphone inside Discord, by Discord's own mute button, and read it back; muted true silences it, false turns it back on. Use when: the person names Discord with the microphone or mic (mute, silence, unmute, turn on). Do not use when: the PC's microphone with no app named (use audio_microphone_mute), speakers or headphones (use audio_mute), what the person hears from a Discord call (use client_deafen_set). Examples: «mute me on discord», «unmute my mic on discord».
tools.clipboard.copy: Copy what is selected in the active window, like Ctrl+C. Use when: copy this or copy the selection. Do not use when: putting a given text in the clipboard (use clipboard_write_text), reading what was copied (use clipboard_read_text), selecting first (use input_select_all). Examples: «copy what's selected», «copy it», «copy this».
tools.clipboard.paste: Paste the clipboard contents where the cursor is, like Ctrl+V. Use when: paste or paste it in. Do not use when: typing a given text (use input_text_type), reading the clipboard aloud (use clipboard_read_text), pasting into an app the person names (use clipboard_paste_into). Examples: «paste here», «paste that», «paste it».
tools.clipboard.paste.into: Paste what the person copied into an application they name: a new document of it is opened (a new note, a new text, a new sheet) and the paste goes there. appId is the application, as for app_open. Use when: paste or put what was copied into an app the person names, new or not. Do not use when: pasting where the cursor already is, no app named (use clipboard_paste). Examples: «paste it into a new Word document», «open a new note and put what I copied there».
tools.clipboard.read.text: Read the text currently in the clipboard, without changing it. It returns up to 6,000 characters (maxCharacters can ask for fewer); truncated and characterCount say when it was cut. Use when: asking what was copied. Do not use when: pasting it somewhere (use clipboard_paste), copying the selection (use clipboard_copy). Examples: «what do I have copied?», «read the clipboard», «what's in my clipboard?».
tools.clipboard.write.text: Put a given text into the clipboard for later pasting, without copying anything from the screen. Use when: the person dictates the text to place in the clipboard. Do not use when: copying the on-screen selection (use clipboard_copy), typing the text directly (use input_text_type). Examples: «copy hello world to the clipboard», «put 'see you at 8' on the clipboard», «save 'done' to the clipboard».
tools.conversation.list: List the conversations with BAXY, the current one and the kept ones from newest to oldest, with each one's id, title and when.
tools.conversation.new: Start a new conversation with BAXY once this answer ends; the current one stays kept.
tools.conversation.open: Go back to a kept conversation, by its id or title from conversation_list, once this answer ends.
tools.conversation.rename: Rename the current conversation, or another one given by its id or title.
tools.desktop.wallpaper.set: Change the desktop wallpaper to a solid color, written as #RRGGBB (blue #004E98, black #000000), or to an image directly in Desktop, Documents, Downloads or Pictures (file_name_invalid otherwise). Use when: change the desktop background or wallpaper. Do not use when: brightness (use system_settings_set). Examples: «change the desktop background to blue», «set beach.jpg from pictures as the background», «change the wallpaper to black».
tools.display.mode.set: Set the main monitor's refresh rate, resolution or both, only to a mode its driver lists (else display_mode_not_listed, nothing changed); read back, and put back when it differs. A resolution alone keeps the refresh rate if listed, else the highest. Use when: change the Hz or the resolution. Do not use when: brightness (use system_settings_adjust), reading the mode (use display_status). Examples: «set the monitor to 75 hz», «resolution to 1280x720».
tools.display.monitor.set: Turn one connected monitor off (active false: it leaves the desktop and Windows moves its windows to the others) or back on (active true), chosen by monitor: its position among the ones on (left, right, above, below, middle), primary (the main one) or secondary (not the main one). With only one monitor on, active false does not take it off: the screen goes dark as Windows darkens it when idle, and a key or mouse move lights it again. Reads the screens back. If which one is unclear, nothing changes and the result lists them: ask. Turning back on with one monitor off needs no monitor. Use when: turn off, disable, turn on or enable a screen or a monitor. Do not use when: resolution or Hz (use display_mode_set), brightness (use system_settings_adjust), locking or turning the PC off (use system_power). Examples: «turn off the left screen» (active false, monitor left), «disable the other screen» (active false, monitor secondary), «turn the monitor back on» (active true), «turn the screen off» (active false), «turn off the screen» (active false).
tools.display.status: Read the connected monitors, on and off: name, position on the desktop (left, right, above, below), which one is the main one, resolution and refresh rate, without changing anything. Use when: asking about monitors, resolution or Hz. Do not use when: brightness (use system_settings_status), general PC specs (use system_status). Examples: «how many monitors do I have?», «what resolution is the screen?», «how many hz is the monitor at?».
tools.document.presentation.create: Create a PowerPoint (.pptx) with a title and 1 to 12 slides (first line the slide's title, the next 8 lines bullets; more lines are left out, bulletLinesLeftOut counts them) in a known folder; more than 12 slides is refused (invalid arguments). Use when: make me a powerpoint or a presentation. Do not use when: Word or Excel (use office_document_create), a plain text file (use file_write). Examples: «make a 5-slide powerpoint about recycling», «create a presentation about Chile», «make a marketing ppt».
tools.email.latest.read: Read the most recent email received in Outlook. Only the newest 100 items of the default Inbox are looked at; a body over 6,000 characters is cut (bodyTruncated, bodyLength). Use when: asking for the last or newest email. Do not use when: replying to it (use email_latest_reply), writing a new email (use email_send). Examples: «read my last email», «what does the last mail say?», «read my latest email».
tools.email.latest.reply: Reply with a given text to the most recent email received in Outlook. Only the newest 100 items of the default Inbox are looked at. The result carries the answered email's body, cut at 6,000 characters (bodyTruncated, bodyLength). Use when: reply to or answer the last email. Do not use when: a new email to an address (use email_send), only reading it (use email_latest_read). Examples: «reply to the last email that I'm running late», «answer the last mail: thanks», «reply ok to the last email».
tools.email.send: Send a new email to an address, with an optional subject, from the owner's Outlook. Without a subject, the first line is used (a first line over 78 characters is cut to 75 and «…»). Use when: an email or mail to a given address with its text. Do not use when: replying to the last email (use email_latest_reply), WhatsApp or Discord (use message_draft), a test send (use message_send_test). Examples: «send an email to juan@gmail.com that I'm not coming tomorrow», «send a mail to ana@empresa.cl with the subject meeting», «send an email to pedro@mail.com: done».
tools.file.compress: Compress a file or folder of the person's into a ZIP with the same name next to it. Only an item directly in Desktop, Documents, Downloads or Pictures (file_name_invalid otherwise). Use when: compressing or zipping. Do not use when: a verified backup of a whole known folder (use backup_known_create). Examples: «compress the photos folder on the desktop», «make a zip of report.docx in documents», «zip project in downloads».
tools.file.edit: Replace an exact piece of text with another in a text file of up to 4 MiB of the person's (Desktop, Documents, Downloads or any folder of their home); the previous version goes to the Recycle Bin. oldText must appear exactly once unless replaceAll is true: copy it exactly as file_read showed it. A name found no time or several times returns at most 5 candidates (candidatesTruncated), looked for 12 levels deep. Use when: change X to Y in a file, fix a line or a word inside a file. Do not use when: writing the whole content (use file_write), adding at the end (use file_write with append), a note (use note_update). Examples: «in notes.txt change Monday to Tuesday», «fix 'helo' to 'hello' in the readme.md», «replace every 2024 with 2025 in report.md».
tools.file.find: List the top level of a folder of the person's (Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures or any folder of their home; without path, Desktop, Documents and Downloads), or find files under it by name (part of it, or a pattern like *.pdf) or by a text inside its text files (20 results by default; a top-level listing shows 50 by default, without hidden and system entries); order recent puts the newest first, order size the largest first (a search by content stops at limit hits and orders only those, so the newest overall may not be among them); each file comes with its folder and relativePath (folder/relativePath is its path for the other file tools) and size in bytes. A search goes 12 folders deep (in the home folder, without hidden or system folders) and a text search reads at most 2,000 files of any kind (only text files of up to 1 MiB for the text); searchScope says what was covered (exhaustive false, the files skipped). timeLimitReached: what it found so far, not all. A view shows 20 at most (truncated, …Shown; the rest is not reached). Use when: what is in a folder (any folder of the person's, whatever its name), the newest files of a folder (order recent), find the file X, where is my X, which file mentions X. Do not use when: BAXY's private work folder (use filesystem_list or filesystem_search), reading a file (use file_read), notes (use note_search), the internet (use web_search). Examples: «what's on the desktop?», «find the budget file», «which file in documents talks about the meeting with Juan?».
tools.file.open: Open a specific file of the person's with its default app or a named installed app. A file not there is not opened: seenElsewhere says in which known folder (folder) and where in it (name) a file of that exact name was seen, so you can open it from there; seenElsewhere looks 4 levels deep in desktop, documents, downloads and pictures, 5 places at most within 3 seconds (searchComplete false: it may be elsewhere too). Only documents, images, audio, video and .zip or .7z files open (file_extension_not_openable). Use when: open the file X, or one your last answer already listed (open it by that name, no file_find). Do not use when: the newest unnamed file (use filesystem_file_open_latest), a folder (use filesystem_folder_open), an application (use app_open), reading without showing (use file_read). Examples: «open homework.docx from the desktop», «open photo.png from downloads with paint», «open report.pdf», «open notes.txt from my Projects folder» → path «Projects\notes.txt». Set foreground true so the person sees the file.
tools.file.read: Read the text of a file of the person's: a text or code file (txt, md, json, code) or a PDF (its own text, no OCR), without opening it on screen. A text file over 4 MiB (known_text_too_large) or a PDF over 64 MiB (known_pdf_too_large) is not read. A long file comes in pages: when hasMore is true, call again with offset set to nextOffset. totalLines (the whole file) and lines (the returned text) are already counted: say those numbers, never count yourself. A name found no time or several times returns at most 5 candidates (candidatesTruncated), looked for 12 levels deep (in the home folder, without hidden or system folders). PDF text extraction stops at 90 seconds (pdf_text_extraction_timeout). Use when: what does it say, summarize or read a named file. Do not use when: showing it on screen (use file_open), a file in BAXY's private work folder (use filesystem_read_text), the open web page (use browser_page_read), a Word or Excel document BAXY created (use office_document_read). Examples: «summarize the pdf contract.pdf», «what is roadmap.md about?», «read me notes.txt from the desktop».
tools.file.write: Write text to a file of the person's (Desktop, Documents, Downloads or any folder of their home): create it, replace one (pass expectedSha256, the fileSha256 file_read gave; the previous version goes to the Recycle Bin), or with append true add the text as a new line at the end. append refuses a file over 10 MiB (file_too_large). Use when: create a text file, write X in a file, add a line at the end of a file. Do not use when: the person names another application to type a stated text in (app_open it, then input_text_type), changing only part of a file (use file_edit), a note (use note_create), Word or Excel (use office_document_create), a PowerPoint (use document_presentation_create). Examples: «create hello.txt on the desktop that says hello», «add 'buy bread' at the end of list.txt», «save this in notes.txt».
tools.filesystem.copy: Copy an already identified file to another path inside BAXY's private work folder, verifying its hash. Use when: copying a sandbox file BAXY listed earlier. Do not use when: a backup (use backup_create), a file of the person's by its name (use filesystem_sandbox_move_named with copy). Examples: «copy that file to the backup folder», «duplicate notes.txt in your work folder», «copy it to another folder».
tools.filesystem.create.directory: Create a new folder of the person's (in Desktop, Documents, Downloads or any folder of their home), with the folders before it that are missing («projects/src»). Use when: create a folder. Do not use when: opening an existing folder (use filesystem_folder_open), creating a file (use file_write). Examples: «create a projects folder on the desktop», «make a new folder called photos in documents», «make a folder homework in downloads».
tools.filesystem.explorer.count: Count the files with an extension directly in a folder: the one path names, or without path the one of the File Explorer window in front (no_explorer_in_front: none in front; explorer_front_not_read or explorer_front_tab_not_known: its folder could not be told; explorer_in_front_shows_no_file_folder: it shows no file folder; then ask which folder). Hidden and system files are not counted. Use when: how many .X files are there. Do not use when: listing or searching files (use file_find), opening the File Explorer itself (use app_open). Examples: «how many .py files are in this folder?», «count the pdfs on the desktop», «how many jpg are here?».
tools.filesystem.file.open.latest: Open the most recently modified document, image, audio, video or .zip/.7z file of a known folder, without the person naming it; programs, installers, disk images and other kinds are skipped, so a newer one of those is not opened. Only files directly in the folder (not its subfolders), hidden and system ones skipped. Use when: the last thing I downloaded or the most recent file. Do not use when: the file is named (use file_open), opening the folder itself (use filesystem_folder_open), listing or showing the newest files without opening one (use file_find with order recent). Examples: «open the last file in downloads», «open the last thing I downloaded», «open the newest file in documents».
tools.filesystem.folder.open: Open a folder of the person's (Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures or any folder of their home) in File Explorer. Use when: open the downloads or documents folder. Do not use when: saying its contents aloud (use file_find), opening a file (use file_open), creating a folder (use filesystem_create_directory). Examples: «open downloads», «open the documents folder for me», «open my pictures folder».
tools.filesystem.known.duplicates: Find duplicate files in Downloads (same size and SHA-256), deleting or changing nothing. 20 groups by default; at most 10,000 files are hashed (candidatesCapped), 12 levels deep. A view shows 20 at most (truncated, …Shown; the rest is not reached). Use when: repeated or duplicate files. Do not use when: deleting a file (use filesystem_known_trash_named), comparing two text files line by line (use filesystem_sandbox_diff_named). Examples: «look for duplicate files in downloads», «do I have repeated files?», «find duplicates in downloads».
tools.filesystem.known.trash.named: Delete a file, or a folder with everything in it (isFolder and entries say so), of the person's (Desktop, Documents, Downloads or any folder of their home) by sending it to the Windows Recycle Bin, where the person can restore it. A name found several times returns at most 5 candidates (candidatesTruncated), looked for 12 levels deep. Use when: delete or remove the file X. Do not use when: emptying the Windows Recycle Bin (use system_recyclebin_empty), a note or task (use note_trash or task_delete), an alarm or reminder (use schedule_alarms). Examples: «delete old.txt from the desktop», «remove photo1.png from downloads», «delete homework.docx».
tools.filesystem.list: List what is in BAXY's private work folder (sandbox), never the person's folders (their home folder and everything under it are file_find). 50 by default (totalCount, hasMore); the ids it gives last 5 minutes. A view shows 20 at most (truncated, …Shown; the rest is not reached). Use when: the person refers to BAXY's own work folder. Do not use when: Desktop, Documents, Downloads or any folder the person names, even one whose name contains BAXY: it is theirs (use file_find). Examples: «what's in your work folder?», «list your work files», «show me the sandbox».
tools.filesystem.move: Move an already identified file to a new path inside BAXY's private work folder, verifying its hash: the destination is the file's whole new path, folder and name («old/notes.txt»), never a folder alone. Use when: moving a work-folder file BAXY listed earlier. Do not use when: the file is only known by its name (use filesystem_sandbox_move_named). Examples: «move that file to the folder called old», «put it in the 2025 subfolder», «move it to archive».
tools.filesystem.read.text: Read the text of an already identified file in BAXY's private work folder. Use when: reading a work-folder file BAXY listed earlier. Do not use when: a text file or PDF in the user's known folders (use file_read). Examples: «read me that file», «what does that txt in your folder say?», «read that file».
tools.filesystem.sandbox.diff.named: Compare two text files in BAXY's private work folder, each by its exact file name, and say which lines differ. Files up to 2 MiB each (sandbox_diff_file_too_large); a view shows 20 changed line numbers (changedLinesShown; changedLineCount is the total, past 100 changedLinesTruncated); lines are compared by position. Use when: compare a with b or how do they differ. Do not use when: finding duplicate files (use filesystem_known_duplicates). Examples: «compare version1.txt with version2.txt», «what changes between notes.txt and old_notes.txt?», «diff of config.json and config2.json».
tools.filesystem.sandbox.move.named: Move, or copy (copy true), a file given by its exact file name: inside BAXY's private work folder, or with path inside that folder of the person's. The destination is the file's whole new path, folder and name («archive/report.txt»), or a folder that already exists; it never replaces a file. Use when: moving or copying a file the person names. Do not use when: the file was already identified by id in the work folder (use filesystem_move). Examples: «move report.txt to the archive folder», «copy notes.txt to backups in documents», «move log.txt to backup».
tools.filesystem.search: Search files by name in BAXY's private work folder (sandbox), not the user's folders. 50 by default (totalCount); links and placeholders are skipped. A view shows 20 at most (truncated, …Shown; the rest is not reached). Use when: searching BAXY's own work folder. Do not use when: Desktop, Documents, Downloads or any folder the person names, even one whose name contains BAXY: it is theirs (use file_find). Examples: «search for report in your work folder», «do you have any log file in your folder?», «search notes in your workspace».
tools.game.catalog.list: List the Steam games installed or downloading on this PC (their local manifests, not the whole library), optionally filtered by text (50 by default; a view shows 20 and totalCount says how many there are). Use when: what games do I have. Do not use when: one game's ownership or install state (use game_entitlement_named or game_installed_named), playing (use game_launch), searching games to find or buy (the store's search: app_open Steam with place results). Examples: «what games do I have on steam?», «list my games», «which games do I have installed on steam?».
tools.game.entitlement.named: Check whether a Steam or Epic game is in the person's library, per the store's local cache (it can miss an owned game), and whether it is installed, without downloading or opening anything. With Steam the title is looked up among the games installed or downloading on this PC and, when none bears it, among the games this Steam client knows (its local cache, not the whole store; titleLookedUpAmong says where it was looked up), and only a title matching exactly one game (case and accents aside) is resolved, otherwise the state is title_not_resolved, which says neither that the game does not exist nor that the person does not own it; with Epic the first cache entry with that title is taken, and a game not found says not_in_local_library_cache (library_cache_unavailable: the cache could not be read; epic_launcher_data_not_found: Epic's data is not on this PC). Use when: do I own it, did I buy it, or is it in my library. Do not use when: only installed-on-disk (use game_installed_named), downloading or installing, even asked as «can you install…?» (use game_install_named), playing (use game_launch), opening Steam itself (use app_open). Examples: «do I have hollow knight on steam?», «is fall guys in my epic library?», «do I own portal 2?».
tools.game.install.cancel: Cancel the partial download of one specific Steam game. Use when: cancel or stop the download of a named game. Do not use when: canceling every download (use game_install_cancel_active), uninstalling (use game_uninstall_named). Examples: «cancel the dota download», «quit downloading cs2», «stop downloading terraria».
tools.game.install.cancel.active: Cancel the downloads Steam has started of games not installed yet; an update of an installed game or a queued install with nothing downloaded is not cancelled, and while one is there the result is steam_downloads_not_covered. Use when: cancel downloads with no game named, or all of them. Do not use when: one specific game is named (use game_install_cancel). Examples: «cancel all the steam downloads», «stop the downloads», «stop all steam downloads».
tools.game.install.named: Download and install a Steam or Epic game by its title. Call it directly, never game_installed_named or game_entitlement_named first: Steam installs only a game the account owns, Epic only one its local entitlement cache shows owned. With Steam only a title matching exactly one game (case and accents aside) is resolved, otherwise steam_title_not_resolved; with Epic the first cache entry with that title is taken (else epic_entitlement_not_verified or epic_install_link_not_resolved; epic_launcher_data_not_found when Epic's library cache is not on this PC or could not be read). Use when: download or install a game. Do not use when: searching or browsing a store (use app_open with place results), only asking whether it is installed or owned (use game_installed_named or game_entitlement_named), checking progress (use game_install_status), a normal program that is not a game (use package_install). Examples: «download hollow knight», «install fall guys on epic», «install terraria from steam».
tools.game.install.status: Check how the download or installation of an already identified Steam game is going. Use when: how is it going or how much is left of a download. Do not use when: asking whether it is installed (use game_installed_named), starting a download (use game_install_named). Examples: «how is the dota download going?», «how much is left for cs2?», «install progress of terraria». Only while a download or install is in progress; whether a game is installed or downloaded at all is game_installed_named. appId: the appId the install or a result gave for that game; never another game's. title: the game the person asked about; the game read is the one with that title (appIdGiven: the appId given was another game's; game_title_mismatch: no game in progress has that title and that appId is another game). An installed game's pending update is its update, not the install.
tools.game.installed.named: Answer only whether a Steam or Epic game is installed on this PC, by its exact name in their manifests, without opening it (a game under another name or from another store is not seen). Use when: the request is a question («is X installed?»). Do not use when: open/play/launch (use game_launch for a game; «open steam» is app_open), library ownership (use game_entitlement_named), normal apps (use app_installed). Examples: «do I have minecraft installed?», «is gta v installed?», «is rocket league installed?». Only for yes/no questions about installation; a request to play or open the game is game_launch.
tools.game.store.page: Open a game's page in the Steam store, by the game's title, and say which game it is. Use when: the page, the store page or the listing of a game the person names. Do not use when: playing it (use game_launch), installing it (use game_install_named), whether it is owned or installed (use game_entitlement_named or game_installed_named). Examples: «I want to see Celeste's listing on steam», «open the Stardew Valley page in the store». Look at the window afterwards to see it arrived.
tools.game.store.search: Search the Steam store with words (a title, a topic or a kind of game) and show its results. Use when: search for games or a game in Steam or its store. Do not use when: what is installed on this PC (use game_catalog_list), one known game's page (use game_store_page). Examples: «find me something with zombies on steam», «see what strategy games there are in the store». Look at the window afterwards to see the results.
tools.game.launch: Launch (play) a Steam game installed on this PC. Use when: play, open or launch a specific game title. Do not use when: opening Steam, Epic or any normal application (use app_open), only asking whether it is installed (use game_installed_named). Examples: «open hollow knight», «I want to play terraria», «launch cs2». appId must be the appId of one game in the installed games list below; never invent an id. If the person said it misheard or spelled differently and one title in the list is clearly that game, use it; if no title in the list is that game, do not launch: say it is not installed. Do not check whether it is installed first. title: the game the person asked for (game_title_mismatch: that appId is another game; its installedGames say which ones are here). A wish to play a game the person names is a launch, not an installed-check.
tools.game.uninstall.named: Uninstall an installed Steam game by its title, after confirmation. Only a title matching exactly one game (case and accents aside) is resolved; otherwise no_steam_manifest_with_that_name (an Epic game: epic_uninstall_not_supported). Use when: uninstall a game. Do not use when: a normal program (use package_uninstall), canceling a download (use game_install_cancel). Examples: «uninstall worms rumble», «delete dota from steam», «uninstall terraria».
tools.input.key.press: Press one key or shortcut in the active window (Enter, Escape, Tab, arrows, Ctrl+S/Z/F/T/W, Ctrl+End/Home: end/start of the whole text, Alt+Tab, F5, Ctrl+Shift+Esc). Use when: a key or shortcut is named. Do not use when: typing text (use input_text_type), select all (use input_select_all), copy or paste (use clipboard_copy or clipboard_paste), clicking a button (use input_visible_click). Examples: «press enter», «hit escape», «do ctrl z». Pass window = the window number from your look at that window, so it acts there and not in the window the person has in front: if it is not in front, BAXY waits for the person's pause and brings it to the front for the act (nothing is sent if Windows does not give it); the front goes back after a text, and after a click or a key at the person's next input; a window the act itself brings up (a new window, another application's) keeps the front; a dialog of that same window (Save As) goes back with it.
tools.input.keyboard.layout: Switch the keyboard input language of the active window to Spanish. Use when: set the keyboard to Spanish. Do not use when: only asking which language it is (use input_keyboard_status), the on-screen keyboard (use input_keyboard_open). Examples: «change the keyboard to Spanish», «set the keyboard to Spanish», «keyboard in spanish please».
tools.input.keyboard.open: Open the Windows on-screen keyboard. Use when: on-screen keyboard or virtual keyboard. Do not use when: changing the keyboard language (use input_keyboard_layout), typing text (use input_text_type). Examples: «bring up the on-screen keyboard», «show me the virtual keyboard», «open on-screen keyboard».
tools.input.keyboard.status: Read the input language of the active window's keyboard, without changing it. Use when: what language is the keyboard in. Do not use when: changing it (use input_keyboard_layout). Examples: «what language is the keyboard in?», «is the keyboard in English?», «current keyboard layout?».
tools.input.pointer.control: Move the mouse pointer to the screen center, click where it is, or scroll down. It cannot drag or draw: it never holds a button down while moving, so clicks leave no line or shape, and no tool drags or draws with the mouse (moving a whole window is window_move or window_snap). Use when: a raw mouse action with no target named. Do not use when: clicking a named button or option (use input_visible_click), scrolling a web page (use browser_control), dragging or drawing. Examples: «click», «move the pointer to the middle of the screen», «scroll downward».
tools.input.scroll: Scroll the active window or a named list or panel up or down by an amount. Use when: go down, go up or scroll in a page, list or document on screen. Do not use when: moving the mouse pointer (use input_pointer_control), clicking a visible option (use input_visible_click). Examples: «move the page down a little», «go up in the list», «scroll down». Pass window = the window number from your look at that window, so it acts there and not in the window the person has in front: if it is not in front, BAXY waits for the person's pause and brings it to the front for the act (nothing is sent if Windows does not give it); the front goes back at the person's next input; a window the act itself brings up (a new window, another application's) keeps the front; a dialog of that same window (Save As) goes back with it.
tools.input.select.all: Select everything in the focused control of the active window, like Ctrl+A. Use when: select everything. Do not use when: copying (use clipboard_copy; select and copy are separate steps). Examples: «select everything», «mark all the text», «select all».
tools.input.text.type: Type a given literal text where the cursor is, in the active window. The text carries no line break or tab: press Enter or Tab with input_key_press. input_text_not_read_back: the keys went in but what the window shows was not read back (a Word document is not): say it was typed without seeing it there. Use when: write or type a stated text. Do not use when: pasting the clipboard (use clipboard_paste), a chat message to someone (use message_draft), writing a file (use file_write), a text to compose for Word (a story, a letter, an essay: use office_document_create, which writes it whole), pressing a key (use input_key_press). Examples: «write hello world», «type good morning». With no window it goes to the window in front, or to the person's window below BAXY's own when BAXY's is in front (the result's surfaceWindow is its number, the window for a key after it); when the person names the application to write in and it is not open, open it first (app_open) and write the stated text there (a text you compose for Word goes to office_document_create). Pass window = the window number from your look at that window, so it acts there and not in the window the person has in front: if it is not in front, BAXY waits for the person's pause and brings it to the front for the act (nothing is sent if Windows does not give it); the front goes back after a text, and after a click or a key at the person's next input; a window the act itself brings up (a new window, another application's) keeps the front; a dialog of that same window (Save As) goes back with it. To change one part of a text already written, pass replacing = that part and text = what goes in its place.
tools.input.visible.click: Click a control or a text you saw in your last look at the window (input_visible_controls), by its label, adding its index when the look gave one. Use when: going to a section, tab or menu of an open app, pressing a button there, or opening a link or result on the page in front of the browser (the page opens it as its own link does: no new tab first). Do not use when: the section is an app_open place (Windows Settings pages, Steam library or store, Discord directs: use app_open with place), you have not looked at the window yet (look first), a raw click where the pointer is (use input_pointer_control), going to a web address (use browser_navigate). Examples: «click OK», «press save», «go into Your Library» (after looking at Spotify). Pass window = the window number from your look, so it acts there: if it is not in front, BAXY waits for the person's pause and brings it forward (nothing is sent if Windows does not give it); the front goes back after a text, and after a click or key at the person's next input; a window the act brings up (a new window, another application's) keeps the front; a dialog of that window (Save As) goes back with it. Without window: with index, in the window of your last look; otherwise in the application you just opened, else in the window the person has in front. It never acts in a window the look marks protected or as a system configuration tool (protected_window).
tools.input.visible.controls: Look at an application window: its visible controls (index, kind, name, state), and the text on screen with includeText (or when the window shows no controls); the view says when the text was not read or was cut. It presses and types nothing; a minimized window is shown behind the one in front, not activated, and the view says so. Use when: you must act inside an open app or read what it shows — before clicking, typing or answering about it, and what it shows of the person (their user name, their status, who is online): BAXY has no account of its own in their apps — or the person asks what is on screen; set application to the app's name (for example right after opening it). Do not use when: the text of a web page is wanted (use browser_page_read), the application named to write in is not open (app_open it first). Examples: «go into Your Library on Spotify» (look at Spotify, then click «Your Library»), «what does the calculator show?», «what buttons are there?», «what name do I appear under in Slack?» (look at Slack with includeText).
tools.media.control: Pause, play, resume, stop, skip to next or go back to previous on what is already playing. Play or pause, whichever applies («play or pause», «stop or play», play/pause, the play key): action toggle, in this one call, with nothing to read or ask first; its result says what it did and what plays now. Use when: pause, next, skip, previous or play, about what is already playing, without naming new content. Do not use when: playing something new by name (use media_play_query, media_play_exact, media_play_youtube or streaming_play_named), seeking seconds (use media_seek_relative), muting (use audio_mute). Examples: «pause the music», «next song», «stop this one and play another» (next), «hit play», «play or pause» (toggle).
tools.media.play.exact: Play one exact song by its title on Spotify, not just open the app: the result titled as title (case, accents and punctuation aside) is played and the now-playing line must name it; a song already playing is left as it is (alreadyPlaying, nothing pressed); with several songs of that title, the topmost titled so plays: to choose the artist, use media_play_query with title and artist. Use when: a precise song title is given. Do not use when: an artist, genre or loose search (use media_play_query), YouTube or a video (use media_play_youtube), a movie or series (use streaming_play_named), only opening Spotify (use app_open). Examples: «put on the song Bohemian Rhapsody», «play exactly Despacito on spotify», «play the song Yellow».
tools.media.play.query: Search music on Spotify (song, artist or style) with query exactly as written and play the first result of Spotify's own search (the result titled as query, case, accents and punctuation aside, when Spotify shows one). The receipt says which control was pressed (selectedControl) and what plays (title, observedNowPlaying), not whether it is what was asked for. Use when: put on or play X, where X is any song, artist, podcast or style, even one you do not know or that sounds misheard: pass X as you heard it. Do not use when: one exact song title (use media_play_exact), YouTube named, even for music, or a video (use media_play_youtube), a movie or series (use streaming_play_named), resuming (use media_control), only opening Spotify (use app_open). Examples: «put on music by bad bunny», «play me some rock on spotify», «play some lofi».
tools.media.play.youtube: Play on YouTube the first video it lists for query, in the person's browser: their default one, or the one given as browser when the person names the browser it plays in; it is verified by the system's media session saying it plays (with browser, only a session of that browser counts). A named browser Windows has not registered opens nothing (named_browser_not_registered) and no other browser takes its place. There is no player of BAXY's own for YouTube; only with no browser named and the default one unable to open does it play in BAXY's own browser. The receipt's browser says where it plays («product» is BAXY's own browser). Use when: a video, or music on YouTube, should play or be watched, in a named browser too. Do not use when: a search the person asks for on YouTube without asking to play or watch («search for X on youtube»): that opens its results page (use browser_navigate, or browser_navigate_named when a browser is named); music on Spotify (use media_play_query or media_play_exact), Netflix, Disney+ or HBO Max titles (use streaming_play_named), only opening YouTube (use browser_navigate). Examples: «put on an origami video on youtube», «play me the dune trailer on youtube», «play lofi on youtube», «put on a cooking video in chrome» → browser chrome.
tools.media.seek.relative: Skip forward or back a number of seconds in what is playing. Use when: skip forward or go back N seconds. Do not use when: next or previous track (use media_control). Examples: «skip ahead 30 seconds», «go back 10 seconds», «skip 1 minute».
tools.media.status: Read what is playing now: title, artist and whether it is paused, without changing anything. Use when: what song is this or what is playing. Do not use when: the volume (use audio_status), playing or pausing (media_control acts with nothing read first). Examples: «what song is playing?», «what is this song called?», «what's playing?».
tools.memory.correct: Correct a fact BAXY already remembers, replacing its value with a new one. Use when: the person fixes a remembered datum. Do not use when: saving a new fact (use memory_save), forgetting it (use memory_forget). Examples: «correction: my favorite color is green», «no, my dog's name is Toby, not Tobi», «update my favorite team to Colo-Colo». Say in your answer what you turned on or changed in memory.
tools.memory.disable: Turn BAXY's memory off so it stops saving and reading facts. Use when: turn off the memory or stop remembering. Do not use when: forgetting specific data (use memory_forget), clearing only this conversation (use memory_session_clear). Examples: «disable your memory», «stop remembering things», «turn off memory». Say in your answer what you turned on or changed in memory.
tools.memory.enable: Turn BAXY's private memory on. Use when: turn on the memory. Do not use when: only asking whether it is on (use memory_status). Examples: «turn on your memory», «start remembering things again», «enable memory». Say in your answer what you turned on or changed in memory.
tools.memory.export: Prepare a private export of what BAXY remembers into Documents, without secret data. Use when: export or make a copy of the memory. Do not use when: just listing it (use memory_list). Examples: «export what you remember», «make me a copy of your memory», «export memory».
tools.memory.forget: Make BAXY forget remembered facts (one fact, a topic, a kind or all), after confirming what is deleted. Use when: forget X or delete what you know about X. Do not use when: only this conversation (use memory_session_clear), turning memory off (use memory_disable), changing a value (use memory_correct). Examples: «forget my address», «delete everything you remember», «forget my birthday». Say in your answer what you turned on or changed in memory.
tools.memory.list: List what BAXY remembers, 20 at most per view (shown and total say how many there are). Use when: a general question about all remembered facts. Do not use when: one concrete thing (use memory_recall), notes (use note_list). Examples: «what things do you remember?», «list your memory», «what do you remember?».
tools.memory.recall: Ask BAXY what it remembers about one concrete thing (5 at most; shown and total say how many there are). Use when: what is my X or do you remember X. Do not use when: everything remembered (use memory_list), searching notes (use note_search). Examples: «what's my favorite color?», «what's my name?», «do you remember my birthday?», «what do you remember about my dog?».
tools.memory.save: Ask BAXY to remember a fact, preference or rule that is not sensitive. At most 512 memories; when full it fails (memory_capacity_reached). Use when: remember that or keep in mind that. Do not use when: sensitive or secret data (use memory_sensitive_save), it must ring or remind at a time (use schedule_alarms), a note (use note_create), a to-do (use task_create). Examples: «remember that my favorite color is blue», «keep in mind that I prefer short answers», «remember my dog's name is Toby». Say in your answer what you turned on or changed in memory.
tools.memory.sensitive.save: Ask BAXY to remember a sensitive or secret datum (health, ID numbers, keys). At most 512 memories; when full it fails (memory_capacity_reached). Use when: the fact to remember is sensitive. Do not use when: an ordinary fact or preference (use memory_save). Examples: «remember my ID number 12.345.678-9», «save that I'm allergic to penicillin», «remember my wifi password». Say in your answer what you turned on or changed in memory.
tools.memory.session.clear: Delete what was remembered for this session only (retention session: since BAXY last started; a new conversation in the panel does not start a new memory session, so it also deletes what was said for the session before it); temporary memories (kept 24 hours) stay until they expire, and permanent memory is kept. Use when: forget what is from this conversation. Do not use when: forgetting permanent facts, or everything about the person (use memory_forget). Examples: «forget what we just talked about», «delete this session's memory», «clear this session». Say in your answer what you turned on or changed in memory.
tools.memory.status: Report whether BAXY's memory is on and what its limits are. Use when: asking if memory is active. Do not use when: listing remembered facts (use memory_list). Examples: «is your memory on?», «can you remember things?», «memory status».
tools.message.draft: Leave a message written for someone in WhatsApp or Discord, unsent; the person sends it. Use when: the person wants it left written without sending (leave it written, without sending). Do not use when: sending it (use message_send), an email (use email_send), a test send (use message_send_test), a greeting for someone, or words for someone there with the person, with no app named (say them yourself in your reply; for a message to pass on with no app named, ask which app). Examples: «leave a message written for Lucía on whatsapp that I'll arrive at 8», «write to Pedro on discord to get online, but don't send it». The recipient is the contact name as the person says it (a name or a family word); never ask for a phone number. WhatsApp opens only a chat named exactly so (case and accents aside); with none or several, nothing is written and the chat list's names come back as candidates (the first 8; candidateCount says how many). Discord opens the first switcher result holding those words (never a voice channel's row: recipient_not_found with that row as observed) and writes only if that chat's title is exactly the name; otherwise nothing is written, that chat stays open and no candidates come back.
tools.message.send: Send a message to someone in WhatsApp or Discord: their chat is opened, the message written, send pressed and the message read back in the chat; the person is always asked first. Use when: send, message or tell X something on whatsapp or discord. Do not use when: it should only be left written (use message_draft), an email (use email_send), a test send (use message_send_test), a greeting for someone, or words for someone there with the person, with no app named (say them yourself in your reply; for a message to pass on with no app named, ask which app). Examples: «send Vicho a whatsapp that I'm on my way», «tell Lucía on whatsapp that I'll arrive at 8», «message Pedro on discord to get online». The recipient is the contact name as the person says it (a name or a family word); never ask for a phone number. WhatsApp sends only to a chat named exactly so (case and accents aside); with none or several, nothing is sent and the chat list's names come back as candidates (the first 8; candidateCount says how many). Discord sends only if the opened chat's title is exactly the name.
tools.message.send.test: Really send a test message or email, always forced to the owner's test channel, never to the person named. Use when: a test message or test email is asked for. Do not use when: a normal message to a contact (use message_draft), a normal email (use email_send). Examples: «send a test message on whatsapp», «send a test email», «test message on discord».
tools.network.dns.status: Read which DNS servers the PC's connection uses. Use when: what DNS do I use. Do not use when: IP addresses (use network_ip_list), general connectivity (use network_status). Examples: «what dns do I have?», «show me the dns servers», «current dns?».
tools.network.ip.list: List this PC's own IP addresses. Use when: what is my IP. Do not use when: DNS servers (use network_dns_status), testing another host (use network_ping). Examples: «what is my ip address?», «tell me my ip addresses», «what's my ip».
tools.network.ping: Ping a host or address once and say whether it answers and how long it takes. Use when: ping or does X answer. Do not use when: general internet connectivity (use network_status). Examples: «ping google.com», «does 8.8.8.8 answer?», «ping cloudflare».
tools.network.port.list: List the PC's open listening TCP and UDP ports. 50 by default (truncated, stableCount). A view shows 20 at most (truncated, …Shown; the rest is not reached). Use when: which ports are open. Do not use when: running programs (use system_process_list). Examples: «which ports do I have open?», «list the listening ports», «open ports?».
tools.network.status: Check whether there is internet connectivity and which network connections are active: online is Windows' own internet check, and connectivity says internet, constrained (a sign-in portal or limited access), local (a network without internet) or none. Use when: do I have internet. Do not use when: Wi-Fi specifically (use wifi_status), pinging a host (use network_ping). Examples: «do I have internet?», «am I connected to the network?», «network status».
tools.note.create: Create a private note with a title and free-text content. At most 512 notes, those in the trash included; when full it fails (note_capacity_reached). Use when: create a note or take a note. Do not use when: the person names another application to type a stated text in (app_open it, then input_text_type), a to-do or list item (use task_create), something that rings or reminds at a time (use schedule_alarms), a fact for BAXY to remember (use memory_save), a text file (use file_write). Examples: «create a note that says buy bread», «take a note: ideas for the thesis», «make a note meeting with Juan».
tools.note.list: List the notes, active or in the trash. 50 by default, but a view shows 20 at most; nextOffset reads on (totalCount says how many). Use when: what notes do I have. Do not use when: searching inside notes (use note_search), tasks (use task_list). Examples: «what notes do I have?», «show me the deleted notes», «list my notes».
tools.note.read: Read one note by its title. Use when: read the note X. Do not use when: searching notes by text (use note_search). Examples: «read the ideas note», «what does the shopping note say?», «read note thesis».
tools.note.restore: Restore a deleted note from the trash, by its title. Use when: recover the note X. Do not use when: a task (use task_restore). Examples: «recover the ideas note», «restore the note I deleted», «undelete note shopping».
tools.note.search: Search the notes that contain a text. 20 by default (totalCount). A view shows 20 at most (truncated, …Shown; the rest is not reached). Use when: search in my notes.
